name: Ganciclovir
executiveSummary: Anti-CMV. Adult induction **5 mg/kg IV every 12 h** × 14–21 days; maintenance **5 mg/kg/day**. Pediatrics similar by kg; congenital CMV often **6 mg/kg every 12 h**. Myelotoxic — monitor CBC.
indications:
## Indications

- CMV disease (retinitis, pneumonitis, colitis, etc.) in immunocompromised/transplant patients.
- Induction/maintenance and high-risk prophylaxis per transplant protocol.
- Symptomatic congenital CMV (specialist regimens).

## Precautions

- Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia — monitor CBC. Teratogenic/potential carcinogen — safe handling.
- Strict renal adjustment. Nephrotoxicity.

> IV only (valganciclovir is the PO form). Infusion ≥ 60 min.

adulto.dose: Induction: **5 mg/kg IV every 12 h** × 14–21 days. Maintenance: **5 mg/kg IV every 24 h** (or **6 mg/kg** 5 days/week per institutional regimen). Transplant prophylaxis: 5 mg/kg/day schemes by risk/center.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute with sterile water; dilute in 50–100 mL NS or 5% dextrose (5–10 mg/mL); infuse **≥ 60 min**. No bolus. Use gloves (cytotoxic).
adulto.notes: Do not refrigerate reconstituted solution on many labels. Adequate hydration.

pediatrico.dose: Induction/treatment: **5 mg/kg IV every 12 h**. Maintenance: **5 mg/kg/day**. Adjust by renal function and transplant protocol.

neonatal.dose: Symptomatic congenital CMV: often **6 mg/kg IV every 12 h** (then step to valganciclovir PO **16 mg/kg every 12 h** in many protocols) — confirm local guidance.
neonatal.notes: Prolonged therapy with hematologic and developmental monitoring.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~12 h room temp (do not refrigerate on many brands). Diluted: ~24 h room temp.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, fever, rash, ↑ creatinine, nausea, potential infertility.
